title: Open-model suitability + fallback strategy walkthrough
summary: Redwood product walkthrough focusing on selecting open models from the catalog, interpreting benchmark sheets, and the compatibility/fallback matrix. Discussed hosted vs dedicated tradeoffs, KV cache and prefix caching, quantization impact, and rollout strategies including canary and automatic fallback. Agreed to run a 2-week pilot benchmark with Atlas sample prompts; Redwood to share benchmark template, security docs, and pricing. Next call scheduled for pilot kickoff.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC) tradeoffs
transcript:
Header: 2026-12-02 16:00 UTC | Duration: 57m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Sam Ortiz (Redwood SE), Liam Patel (Atlas CTO), Priya Desai (Atlas ML Eng), Noah Kim (Atlas SRE)
Links shared: deck: https://redwood.example/decks/open-model-suitability, bench sheet: https://sheets.example/atlas-pilot

Summary (auto): quick run through of catalog UI, heuristics for model choice, and fallback rules.

[00:00] Maya - Redwood (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, we're gonna run through how you'd pick open models in the catalog, and how to configure fallbacks so your storefront doesn't blow up if a larger model flaps out.
[00:18] Liam - Atlas: Thanks Maya. Quick context — we're migrating product search generation and some conversational assistants off local LLM infra; main concerns are p95 latency under 600ms, predictable cost, and data isolation for PII.
[00:30] Sam - Redwood (SE): Great, that's helpful. We'll show catalog filters for latency and cost buckets, then demo how the compatibility matrix flags quantization/hybrid kernels.
[00:45] Priya - Atlas: Awesome. Also SOC2 and KMS questions up front — we will need audit logs and customer-managed keys if we go private.
[00:55] Maya: Yep we'll cover that at the end. Quick note: some product names in the UI might show as "Redwod verified" in the transcript — the deck's accurate.

[02:10] Sam: Ok launching the console — top-left is the model catalog, you can filter for architecture, target latency, and verified benchmarks. Here's an example: 'bertish-7b' shows p50 90ms on A100 80GB but p95 is 420ms. It also lists quantization options; the compat column says "FP16 -> int8 OK (kernel: qk-matv)" — some of the kernel names are low-level but necessary for runtime planning.
[03:05] Priya: When you say p95 420ms that's for what batch size?
[03:12] Sam: That's batch=1, typical conversational traffic. We also show throughput curves at batch sizes 1,4,8 in the bench sheet.
[03:30] Noah: Do you auto-choose the kernel at runtime? Our ops team wants deterministic scheduling.
[03:36] Sam: The runtime picks optimized kernels based on the model and observed sequence length distributions; you can also pin kernels per model if you want determinism. That's what Dedicated customers often do.

[05:00] Liam: Talk through fallback — if a pinned 13B model is saturated, do you transparently fall back to a 7B?
[05:15] Maya: Yes, we have routing policies: you can set hard fallbacks (always try primary, else fallback) or progressive routing (try primary for low latency gates, then fallback). You can also route by token budget — e.g. if remaining allowance < X tokens, go to cheaper variant.
[05:40] Priya: How do you handle output consistency — user-visible regression when switching models?
[05:48] Sam: We recommend prompt templates and a small eval set tied to alerts. Redwood Optimize can surface regression alerts when quality metrics degrade after a fallback. Also canary rollouts let you funnel a percent of traffic to new model variants and measure drift.

[07:20] Speaker 1 (automated): [some audio glitch]...
[07:35] Maya: Sorry, just a quick aside, the bench sheet link has sample prompts from your vector search use case if we wanna align the pilot.

[10:00] Sam: Let's open a compatibility matrix row: here 'libra-13b' shows GPU support: A100-80GB yes, H100 autop; quantization: 8-bit int OK but attention block size may need custom kernel; sequence length tests show p95 jumps after 1k tokens. Notes: "KV cache warmup can add 30-50ms first request" (transcription might say 'kay cache').
[11:22] Priya: The 'KV cache warmup' — can you persist KV across sessions to avoid warmups?
[11:28] Sam: We support persistent KV caches for sessionized flows on Dedicated and Private. On Hosted you can enable prefix caching which reduces repetition costs.

[13:10] Liam: Security — what's the onboarding for Private (VPC)? Encryption keys?
[13:18] Maya: For Private we offer a control plane with customer VPC connectivity; KMS integrations (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault), HSM optional. We'll send SOC2 package and our network diagram.
[13:35] Noah: Does your audit log include per-token request traces?
[13:40] Sam: We have token-level billing and request traces that include route, model version, and timings — we can redact prompt text from logs if needed for compliance.

[16:05] Priya: Show me an example bench interpretation — what should we pay attention to?
[16:12] Sam: Focus on p50/p95 latency, cost per 1k tokens, and memory headroom for concurrency. For example, model A had p50 60ms p95 340ms cost $0.015/1k tokens; model B p50 120ms p95 520ms but cost $0.007/1k tokens. Depending on tail latency SLO you choose.
[17:00] Priya: For search ranking generative rerankers we need p95 < 350ms, so model A fits but the cost is twice.
[17:15] Maya: That's where batching and prefix caching can help reduce unit cost while keeping latency. We can also recommend quantized variants that are 20-30% cheaper at slight quality delta.

[20:00] Liam: Can you run an on-prem micro-bench with our sample workload?
[20:08] Maya: Yes, pilot is 2 weeks: Atlas provides ~2k representative prompts, Redwood runs bench across 3 candidate models, returns p50/p95, cost estimate, and a suggested fallback matrix.
[20:24] Noah: Timeline for pilot?
[20:28] Maya: We can kick off next week pending NDA and pilot data. Deliverables within 10 business days after data ingest.

[22:40] Sam: Quick demo of routing UI — here's a route: primary=libra-13b (pinned ver v1.2), fallback=libra-7b quant8, route rule = if queue_depth>8 or latency>500ms then fallback; also secondary fallback to 'tiny-2b' for best-effort. You can set rollout percentages and automatic rollback thresholds.
[23:20] Priya: In that routing rule, is latency measured end-to-end including network?
[23:25] Sam: Yes it measures end-to-end at the ingress point configured for you; on Private that's your VPC ingress so network hops reduce.

[25:10] Maya: Objection we hear a lot: "we cannot accept model non-determinism and output drift when falling back". The recommended pattern: maintain a small golden eval for user-visible prompts and run shadow traffic through fallback model to detect regressions before switching traffic.
[25:35] Liam: Makes sense. Also curious on pricing for Dedicated reserved capacity.
[25:42] Maya: Pricing is usage + reserved capacity commitment. We'll share a simple example in the pricing doc but pilot results will give you a better commit number.

[28:00] Speaker 2: [mumbling]
[28:12] Priya: A small question on model assets — if we bring our finetuned model, how's onboarding?
[28:20] Sam: You can upload model artifacts to the private registry or provide a container; we validate architecture and provide a kernel compatibility report. For some finetuned LLMs we may need to generate a new kernel mapping — that's usually 2-3 days for our engineering bench.

[31:05] Noah: Are competitors like OpenAI or Anthropic mentioned in contract lists? We evaluate them for accuracy but your fallback policy is attractive.
[31:20] Maya: We often see customers use OpenAI for general models and Redwood-managed open models for cost control. We'll include a short competitor notes doc.

[33:40] Sam: Ok run through of Canary example: 5% traffic to new model variant, monitor quality metrics and p95, if quality delta>threshold auto rollback. You can tie thresholds to eval prompts.
[34:10] Priya: Does Redwood provide tooling to collect outputs and run automatic A/B stats?
[34:16] Sam: Yes, Optimize has an eval harness, side-by-side diffs, and regression alerting. We'll show you the UI in the pilot dashboard.

[36:50] Liam: On data residency — our EU customers' PII cannot leave region. How do you ensure regional model hosting?
[36:58] Maya: We can pin region at deployment time; Private is best for strict residency. Hosted can be region-restricted depending on availability zones.

[39:00] Speaker 1: [background noise] Sorry.
[39:12] Priya: Anything about tokenization differences across models — we saw odd length delta when switching from a t5-based model to llama-deriv.
[39:22] Sam: Tokenization differences can cause cost variance. The catalog shows tokenization family and estimated tokens for your sample prompts in the bench sheet.

[42:00] Maya: Quick recap and next steps — we'll run pilot, share security docs, and pricing. Any final questions?
[42:18] Liam: One: will you include example nginx that covers tracing headers?
[42:24] Sam: Yes we'll drop a sample ingress proxy with tracing header examples and a small snippet to redact prompts in logs.

[44:00] Priya: Also, can we request model shortlist suggestion based on our prompt set?
[44:07] Maya: Absolutely. Send the sample prompts and we'll return a ranked shortlist with expected latency/cost and a compatibility matrix.

[46:30] Noah: Action on our side: get NDA signed and logistics for data transfer.
[46:38] Liam: Also, cost center approval — procurement will need a one-pager.

[50:00] Maya: OK we'll send: 1) Bench template, 2) SOC2/network diagram/KMS note, 3) pricing example, 4) pilot SOW draft.
[50:12] Priya: Sounds good. Let's reconvene for pilot kickoff — how about 2026-12-09?
[50:20] Maya: Works for us.

[56:00] Maya: Thanks all, we'll follow up via email with links and action items.

[56:30] End of recording
